# Feature: `ask` Pipeline (rule-based)

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-007
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan.md` (row FEAT-007; §3 search fast-path rationale; §5 CLI surface; §7 architectural decisions on `SearchProvider` strategy and ephemeral profiles)

This feature is the **first user-visible slice** of Yantra. A user types

```
yantra ask "today's top news on AI"
```

and gets back one or more **AskCard**s — each carrying a summary, the source URL, the fetch timestamp, and a quoted snippet from the source. The pipeline is `search → fetch → extract → summarize → render`, with each stage swappable behind an interface (`SearchProvider`, `ContentFetcher`, `Extractor`, `Summarizer`, `Renderer`).

The headline invariant is **agent-optional**: `ask` ships fully functional with `--no-llm`. The rule-based summarizer (first-N-sentences + heuristic ranking, falling back to lede) is the default path; the LLM-enhanced summarizer is a **seam** stubbed in this feature and lit up in FEAT-011. CI matrix legs `LLM_PROVIDER=none` exercise the entire `ask` surface and must pass on all three OSes from the day this feature merges.

**Concrete latency targets** (cold cache, single query, p95):

- API fast-path (Tavily or Brave configured): **≤ 8 s** end-to-end, top-3 cards.
- Browser-only fallback (no API key configured): **≤ 30 s** end-to-end, top-3 cards.
- Warm cache hit (same query within 24 h): **≤ 1.5 s** end-to-end.

These targets are enforced by a `@requires-network` integration test running against a fixture HTTP server (latency budget assertions) and a `@no-llm` micro-benchmark in CI nightly.

**Why this feature now.** Per plan §2: "After FEAT-007 the user has a working `ask`." This is the proof the spine works: protocol types from FEAT-002 carry a real `TaskRequest` through a real executor flow (FEAT-005's verbs are not invoked, but the `TaskEvent` emitter is reused), the BrowserProvider from FEAT-003 is exercised in its ephemeral mode, the sanitizer chokepoint from FEAT-006 is the only path any future LLM-bound content can take, and the ethics gate is non-bypassable on every fetched URL. The result is a useful product even with `LLM_PROVIDER=none`.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

### On-Disk Artifacts

A successful `ask` produces one **run directory** under `~/.local/share/yantra/runs/<run-id>/` (the canonical observability artifact per memory §Logging; layout owned by FEAT-005). For this feature the directory contains:

```
~/.local/share/yantra/runs/<run-id>/
  manifest.json         # { task_id, type: "ask", query, search_provider, started_at, finished_at, status, scope_summary: "public" }
  events.jsonl          # TaskEvent stream — one line per stage transition
  agent.jsonl           # populated only when LLM-enhanced path was used (FEAT-011); otherwise empty
  secrets.jsonl         # one entry per keychain lookup (tavily.api_key / brave.api_key), value NEVER recorded
  outputs.json          # { cards: AskCard[] } — the canonical result the renderer rendered
  cards/                # one <index>.json per card, identical content to outputs.cards[i] for easy diffing
  fetched/              # one <sha256(url)>.html.txt per fetched page (gzipped if > 16 KiB), retention 7 days
  report.md             # human-readable summary; one section per card with quoted snippet + source link
```

The **AskCache** lives outside the run directory at `~/.cache/yantra/ask/<sha256(query + "|" + provider + "|" + utc_day)>.json`:

```jsonc
// ~/.cache/yantra/ask/<hash>.json
{
  "version": 1,
  "query": "today's top news on AI",
  "search_provider": "tavily",
  "utc_day": "2026-05-11",
  "created_at": "2026-05-11T10:14:00.000Z",
  "ttl_seconds": 86400,
  "cards": [
    /* AskCard[] */
  ],
}
```

- Cache directory permissions: **0700** (owner-only). On Windows, equivalent ACL via `fs.promises.chmod` is best-effort; the cache is gated behind a `yantra doctor` warning when the dir is world-readable on POSIX.
- Cache key is **`sha256(query + "|" + provider + "|" + utc_day)`** — the day component is the UTC date string from `started_at`, so the cache invalidates at UTC-midnight rollover. `--no-cache` bypasses both read and write.
- Per-entry TTL is 24 h; on read, expired entries are removed lazily.
- Total cache size is soft-capped at 100 MB; oldest-first eviction when exceeded.

### In-Memory Entities

Defined in `packages/core/src/extraction/types.ts` (single file owns the shared shapes; the per-stage modules consume them).

```ts
// AskQuery — the parsed user request flowing through the pipeline.
export interface AskQuery {
  readonly raw: string; // verbatim user input
  readonly normalized: string; // trimmed, single-spaced, lowercase for cache key
  readonly limit: number; // top-K cards to return (default 3, max 10)
  readonly noCache: boolean;
  readonly noLlm: boolean; // honors --no-llm flag AND LLM_PROVIDER=none env
  readonly budgetCalls: number | null; // null = unbounded; otherwise hard cap on fetches
  readonly searchProvider: SearchProviderName | null; // null = auto-select
  readonly perFetchTimeoutMs: number; // default 8_000
  readonly pipelineBudgetMs: number; // default 30_000
}

// SearchResult — one row returned by a SearchProvider, before fetch.
export interface SearchResult {
  readonly url: string; // canonical (https where possible)
  readonly title: string | null; // null when provider doesn't supply
  readonly snippet: string | null; // provider-supplied excerpt; may be untrusted (sanitized for any LLM use)
  readonly source: SearchProviderName; // for provenance in audit log
  readonly rank: number; // 0-indexed position from provider
  readonly publishedAt: string | null; // ISO-8601 when provider supplies
}

// FetchedDoc — the raw bytes from a URL plus metadata; the input to the extractor.
export interface FetchedDoc {
  readonly url: string;
  readonly finalUrl: string; // after redirects
  readonly fetchedAt: string; // ISO-8601 UTC
  readonly contentType: string | null; // e.g., "text/html; charset=utf-8"
  readonly html: string; // never the raw Buffer — decoded to UTF-8 here
  readonly statusCode: number;
  readonly fetchMode: 'http' | 'browser'; // which fetcher path served it
  readonly elapsedMs: number;
}

// ExtractedArticle — the result of running Readability over a FetchedDoc.
export interface ExtractedArticle {
  readonly url: string;
  readonly title: string | null;
  readonly byline: string | null;
  readonly publishedAt: string | null; // best-effort parse from <time>, <meta>, JSON-LD
  readonly siteName: string | null;
  readonly contentText: string; // plain text (Readability `textContent`)
  readonly contentHtml: string; // cleaned HTML (Readability `content`); never sent to LLM raw
  readonly excerpt: string | null; // Readability `excerpt`
  readonly lengthChars: number;
}

// AskCard — the renderable artifact, one per source.
export interface AskCard {
  readonly url: string; // canonical link to source
  readonly title: string; // article title or fallback to host + path
  readonly source: string; // host portion of url
  readonly fetchedAt: string; // ISO-8601 — auditable "as of"
  readonly publishedAt: string | null;
  readonly summary: string; // rule-based: first-N-sentences (default 3); LLM-enhanced when lit up
  readonly summaryKind: 'rule-based' | 'llm-enhanced' | 'fallback-lede';
  readonly quotedSnippet: string; // a verbatim ≤ 280-char excerpt for user verification
  readonly tags: readonly string[]; // ["news", "ai"] — heuristic, lowercase
  readonly notice: string | null; // user-visible disclaimer (e.g., "LLM synthesis unavailable", "fetch timed out", "source skipped: robots")
}

// SearchProviderName — closed enum for audit + config selection.
export type SearchProviderName = 'tavily' | 'brave' | 'browser';
```

### Repository-Style Interfaces

All four interfaces are pure abstractions; concrete impls are constructor-injected (memory §Design Patterns — Strategy + Repository-like).

```ts
// packages/core/src/extraction/search/provider.ts
export interface SearchProvider {
  readonly name: SearchProviderName;
  search(
    query: string,
    opts: { limit: number; signal: AbortSignal },
  ): Promise<readonly SearchResult[]>;
}

// packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.ts
export interface ContentFetcher {
  fetch(url: string, opts: { timeoutMs: number; signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<FetchedDoc>;
}

// packages/core/src/extraction/readability.ts
export interface Extractor {
  extract(doc: FetchedDoc): Promise<ExtractedArticle | null>; // null = unrecoverable parse failure
}

// packages/core/src/extraction/cache.ts
export interface AskCache {
  get(key: string): Promise<readonly AskCard[] | null>;
  put(key: string, cards: readonly AskCard[]): Promise<void>;
  delete(key: string): Promise<void>;
}

// packages/core/src/extraction/summarizer.ts
export interface Summarizer {
  summarize(
    article: ExtractedArticle,
    query: AskQuery,
  ): Promise<{ summary: string; kind: AskCard['summaryKind'] }>;
}
```

`SearchProvider` is the **strategy** referenced in plan §7. The selector function (TASK-004) returns one of three concrete impls based on config + keychain probing.

### Relationships

- An `AskQuery` produces N `SearchResult`s (typically 5–10 from the provider; top-`limit` are followed).
- Each followed `SearchResult` produces 0 or 1 `FetchedDoc` (0 = ethics refusal, timeout, or HTTP error → emit failure card).
- Each `FetchedDoc` produces 0 or 1 `ExtractedArticle` (0 = Readability returned `null` → emit failure card).
- Each `ExtractedArticle` produces exactly 1 `AskCard`. Each failure also produces exactly 1 `AskCard` (with `notice` filled and an empty `summary`) — **the pipeline never silently drops a result row**; per-source failures appear in the deck rather than failing the whole ask.
- The `AskCache` is keyed by `(query, provider, utc_day)` and stores the full `AskCard[]` deck.

### Future DB Schema (Phase 2 — informational only)

When the Phase 2 daemon adds SQLite, these three tables forward-compat the on-disk shape:

```sql
-- All fields nullable EXCEPT id, query, started_at; preserves no-op upgrade from filesystem
CREATE TABLE ask_queries (
  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- task_id (ULID)
  query           TEXT NOT NULL,
  search_provider TEXT NOT NULL,              -- "tavily" | "brave" | "browser"
  started_at      TEXT NOT NULL,              -- ISO-8601
  finished_at     TEXT,
  status          TEXT NOT NULL,              -- "ok" | "partial" | "failed"
  no_llm          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  budget_calls    INTEGER,
  run_dir         TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE ask_cards (
  query_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES ask_queries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  rank            INTEGER NOT NULL,
  url             TEXT NOT NULL,
  title           TEXT NOT NULL,
  source          TEXT NOT NULL,
  fetched_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  published_at    TEXT,
  summary         TEXT NOT NULL,
  summary_kind    TEXT NOT NULL,
  quoted_snippet  TEXT NOT NULL,
  tags            TEXT NOT NULL,              -- JSON array
  notice          TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (query_id, rank)
);

CREATE TABLE ask_cache (
  cache_key       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- sha256(query|provider|utc_day)
  query           TEXT NOT NULL,
  search_provider TEXT NOT NULL,
  utc_day         TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  ttl_seconds     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  payload_json    TEXT NOT NULL               -- serialized AskCard[]
);
```

The MVP filesystem layout serializes to these rows trivially — no destructive migration needed.

## 3. Files

Exhaustive list of files this feature creates (paths repo-relative; all under `packages/core/src/extraction/` unless noted).

**Core types & orchestrator**

- `packages/core/src/extraction/types.ts` — the shared shapes from §2 (`AskQuery`, `SearchResult`, `FetchedDoc`, `ExtractedArticle`, `AskCard`, `SearchProviderName`). Pure types; zero runtime imports beyond `node:crypto` for the cache-key helper, which lives in its own file.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/ask-pipeline.ts` — the orchestrator (`AskPipeline.run(query, opts)` → `Promise<AskCard[]>`). Wires `SearchProvider` → `ContentFetcher` → `Extractor` → `Summarizer` → `Renderer`. Emits `TaskEvent`s per stage (reusing the `events` module from FEAT-005). Honors `pipelineBudgetMs` via a top-level `AbortController`.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/cache.ts` — `FileSystemAskCache` implementing `AskCache`. SHA-256 keying, 24 h TTL, 0700 dir perms (best-effort on Windows), 100 MB size cap with oldest-first eviction.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/cache-key.ts` — `cacheKey(query, provider, utcDay) → string` (sha256 hex). Single source of truth.

**Search**

- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/provider.ts` — `SearchProvider` interface + `SearchProviderName` re-export + the **provider-selector** function `selectSearchProvider(config, keychain, browserProvider, logger) → SearchProvider` (auto-detect API keys; fall back to browser). Selector is the only export consumed by the orchestrator.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/tavily.ts` — `TavilySearchProvider`. POST `https://api.tavily.com/search` via `undici.request`; reads `tavily.api_key` from keychain at construction time; maps response to `SearchResult[]`; handles 401/403 → `TavilyAuthError`, 429 → `RateLimitError` (caller falls through to next provider per TASK-004).
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/brave.ts` — `BraveSearchProvider`. GET `https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search` with `X-Subscription-Token` header from `brave.api_key`; maps response; same error classes.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/browser.ts` — `BrowserSearchProvider`. Uses `BrowserProvider` from FEAT-003 to launch an ephemeral context, navigates to DuckDuckGo HTML (`https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q=<encoded>`) — chosen over Google for two reasons: (a) HTML endpoint requires no JS, (b) DDG's robots.txt explicitly permits this path. Extracts top-N result `<a class="result__a">` nodes via the locator engine (FEAT-004) and parses them into `SearchResult[]`. The single fetch URL passes through the ethics gate.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/errors.ts` — `TavilyAuthError`, `RateLimitError`, `BrowserSearchError` extending a shared `SearchProviderError extends Error` (per memory §Error Handling — custom error classes carry context).

**Fetch & extract**

- `packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.ts` — `HttpFetcher` (primary, via `undici.request` with a polite UA `"YantraBot/0.1 (+https://yantra.dev/bot)"`, follows up to 5 redirects, 8 s default per-fetch timeout, hard cap on body at 5 MB) + `BrowserFallbackFetcher` (uses BrowserProvider for sites detected as JS-heavy: heuristic = HTML body < 10 KiB AND has `<script src=` references AND no `<article>` / `<main>` semantic root). Together they compose a `HybridContentFetcher` implementing `ContentFetcher` that delegates by heuristic.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/readability.ts` — wraps `@mozilla/readability` (constructed against a `jsdom` `Window` — Readability needs a real DOM; we use `jsdom` here specifically rather than `cheerio` because Readability's API requires `Document`. Cheerio is used **inside** this module to pre-clean the DOM: strip `<nav>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>`, `<form>`, role=banner/contentinfo, and known cookie-banner classes before handing to Readability). Implements `Extractor`. Returns `null` cleanly when Readability gives up (no throw).

**Summarize**

- `packages/core/src/extraction/summarizer.ts` — `RuleBasedSummarizer` implementing `Summarizer`. Algorithm:
  1. Use `Intl.Segmenter` (Node 24.15.0 native) to split `contentText` into sentences.
  2. Score each of the first 8 sentences: position-weight (earlier = higher), query-term overlap (case-folded), presence of capitalized multi-word phrases (cheap proxy for named entities, no NER dependency).
  3. Pick top N (default 3) by score, then re-sort by original position to preserve reading flow.
  4. If `contentText` < 200 chars OR no sentences scored above threshold, fall back to `excerpt` (Readability) → `lede` (first 280 chars) — emit `summaryKind: "fallback-lede"`.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/llm-summarizer.ts` — `LlmSummarizer` **STUB**. Exports the class and the factory `createLlmSummarizer(llmClient | null, sanitizer)`. The factory returns `null` when `llmClient` is null OR `process.env.LLM_PROVIDER === 'none'` OR the query has `noLlm: true`. The real implementation is added in FEAT-011 (this feature contains the type, the seam, and a `// FEAT-011:` marker comment; the import path is stable). Behind a feature gate (`features.llmSummarize` in config, default `false` in MVP) so FEAT-011 turns it on by config flip rather than code edit.

**Render**

- `packages/core/src/extraction/card.ts` — `AskCard` re-export (lives in `types.ts`; this file is the renderer entrypoint) + three renderers:
  - `renderTerminal(cards, opts) → string` — ASCII box per card (no `boxen` runtime dep; we draw boxes ourselves to keep `packages/core` lean), color via `picocolors` (already a transitive dep of vitest, single-import safe).
  - `renderJson(cards) → object` — stable shape for `--json`; matches `outputs.json` exactly.
  - `renderMarkdown(cards) → string` — used for `report.md`; one `##` heading per card with link, source, fetched-at, quoted block.

**Cross-cutting glue**

- `packages/core/src/extraction/ethics-adapter.ts` — thin adapter that wraps the ethics gate (owned by FEAT-005) so the pipeline doesn't import FEAT-005 internals; takes `{ checkUrl }` callback, returns a `BlockedUrl` decision the pipeline turns into a "source skipped" card.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/index.ts` — barrel re-exporting the public surface (`AskPipeline`, `AskCard`, types, `selectSearchProvider`).

**CLI binding**

- `apps/cli/src/commands/ask.ts` — `commander` subcommand for `yantra ask "<query>"`. Parses flags (`--json`, `--no-llm`, `--no-cache`, `--budget`, `--search-provider`, `--limit`). Constructs the pipeline, runs it, streams events to stderr, prints renderer output to stdout. Maps pipeline errors to exit codes per memory §Error Handling (1 validation, 2 execution, 3 environment).

**Tests (mirrored under `packages/core/src/extraction/` co-located)**

- `packages/core/src/extraction/types.spec.ts` — `@no-llm` AAA tests for any helpers that live with types (cache-key purity).
- `packages/core/src/extraction/cache-key.spec.ts` — `@no-llm` + fast-check property: same `(query, provider, utc_day)` triple → identical key; different triples → different key.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/cache.spec.ts` — `@no-llm`; TTL expiry, size-cap eviction, 0700 perms (POSIX only via `it.runIf(process.platform !== 'win32')`).
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/tavily.spec.ts` — `@no-llm`; mocks `undici` via `MockAgent`; covers happy path, 401, 429, malformed response.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/brave.spec.ts` — `@no-llm`; same shape as Tavily.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/browser.spec.ts` — `@no-llm`; uses a `FakeBrowserProvider` test double; asserts DDG URL composition + ethics gate is called.
- `packages/core/src/extraction/search/provider.spec.ts` — `@no-llm`; provider selector exercises all four config × keychain combinations (config=`tavily`+key present → Tavily; config=`tavily`+missing key → fallback browser + warning; config=`auto`+both keys → Tavily preferred; config=`auto`+no keys → browser).
- `packages/core/src/extraction/fetcher.spec.ts` — `@no-llm`; `MockAgent` for HTTP; `FakeBrowserProvider` for fallback; asserts heuristic triggers correctly.

- `e2e/ask-no-llm.spec.ts` — same fixture, runs with `LLM_PROVIDER=none`. **This is the headline test for the agent-optional invariant.**

## 4. Dependencies

### Upstream features

- **FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI)** — workspace, test tags, CI matrix.
- **FEAT-002 (Yantra Protocol v0)** — `TaskRequest`, `TaskEvent` types; this feature emits a fixed subset of events (`task_started`, `step_started`/`step_completed` per stage, `task_completed` / `task_failed`).
- **FEAT-003 (Chrome Launcher & BrowserProvider)** — ephemeral context for `BrowserSearchProvider` and the JS-fallback fetcher.
- **FEAT-005 (Plan Executor & Step Verbs)** — only the **ethics gate** is reused here (via the `ethics-adapter`); the executor's verbs are not invoked by `ask` (this is the "single shot pipeline" path, not a workflow replay).
- **FEAT-006 (Security Envelope)** — the **sanitizer chokepoint** is the only path the FEAT-011 LLM-enhanced summarizer is permitted to take; this feature wires the seam (LLM summarizer takes sanitizer in its constructor) even though it returns `null` in MVP. Keychain abstraction from FEAT-006 reads `tavily.api_key` / `brave.api_key`.

### External npm dependencies (latest stable, per memory §Dependencies)

Runtime, added to `packages/core/package.json`:

- `@mozilla/readability` — article extraction.
- `jsdom` — DOM construction for Readability (Readability requires a real `Document`).
- `cheerio` — pre-clean pass before Readability + lightweight DOM ops in `BrowserSearchProvider` result parsing.
- `undici` — HTTP client (Node native; pinned latest stable).
- `picocolors` — ANSI color in terminal renderer (zero deps, ~2 KB).

Dev/test, added to `packages/core/package.json`:

- `fast-check` — property tests for cache-key and summarizer determinism (memory §Testing).
- `undici` already ships `MockAgent` — no extra dep for HTTP mocking.

`node-html-parser` is **not** chosen (TBD resolved): we use `cheerio` for pre-clean (more familiar API, broader ecosystem) and `jsdom` for Readability (required). The native `node:html` API does not exist in Node 24.15.0 (the original TBD); this clarification is recorded here.

Each task is a vertical slice with implementation, unit tests, and a documentation update. - [ ] **Implementation**: Create `search/provider.ts` (interface only) and `search/tavily.ts`. Adds `search/errors.ts` with `SearchProviderError`, `TavilyAuthError`, `RateLimitError`. Honors `signal: AbortSignal` by passing to `undici.request`'s `signal` option.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `search/tavily.spec.ts` with `MockAgent`: happy path (200 + 3 results → 3 `SearchResult`), 401 → `TavilyAuthError`, 429 → `RateLimitError`, malformed JSON → `SearchProviderError` with parse context. All `@no-llm`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: `packages/core/README.md` adds an "Extraction" section listing the pluggable provider strategy.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- tavily` exits 0 with 4 passing tests; `pnpm --filter @yantra/core typecheck` clean.

### TASK-002: `BraveSearchProvider` impl

- [ ] **Implementation**: `search/brave.ts`. GET `https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search?q=<encoded>&count=<limit>` with header `X-Subscription-Token: <key>` and `Accept: application/json`. Reads `brave.api_key` from keychain. Maps `web.results[]` → `SearchResult[]` (provider-supplied `url`, `title`, `description` → `snippet`, `age` → `publishedAt` when parseable to ISO).
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `search/brave.spec.ts` mirrors Tavily structure (happy path, 401, 429, malformed). All `@no-llm`.

- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- brave` passes; brave + tavily tests run in parallel without interfering (no shared module-level state).

### TASK-003: `BrowserSearchProvider` impl (DuckDuckGo HTML)

- [ ] **Implementation**: `search/browser.ts`. Constructor takes `{ browserProvider, ethicsGate, logger }`. `search(query)` flow:
  1. Compute `url = "https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q=" + encodeURIComponent(query)`.
  2. Pass `url` through `ethicsGate.checkUrl(url)`; on refusal, throw `BrowserSearchError("ethics-refused", { host, reason })`.
  3. Launch ephemeral browser context (per-call profile under `os.tmpdir() + "/yantra-search-<uuid>"`, removed on completion).
  4. Navigate, `wait_for` selector `.result__a` (5 s timeout — DDG HTML endpoint is fast).
  5. Extract top-`limit` `<a class="result__a">` nodes; for each, capture `href` and `textContent`; sibling `.result__snippet` becomes `snippet`.
  6. Return `SearchResult[]` with `source: "browser"`, `rank` = index, `publishedAt: null` (DDG HTML doesn't expose it).

### TASK-010: `FileSystemAskCache` impl

- [ ] **Implementation**: `cache.ts` + `cache-key.ts`. `cacheKey(query, provider, utcDay)` is `sha256(query.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').toLowerCase() + '|' + provider + '|' + utcDay)` hex-encoded. `FileSystemAskCache` constructor takes `{ dir: string; ttlSeconds: number; maxBytes: number; logger: Logger }`. On first use ensures the dir exists with mode 0o700 (POSIX). `get(key)` reads `<dir>/<key>.json`, checks `created_at + ttl_seconds < now` → returns `null` and lazy-deletes; otherwise returns the deserialized `cards`. `put(key, cards)` serializes + writes atomically (`tmpfile` → `rename`). After every `put`, opportunistically evicts oldest entries until total bytes ≤ `maxBytes`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `cache.spec.ts` (POSIX-gated where perms-tested; Windows runs everything else):
  - put → get round-trip
  - TTL expiry returns `null` and deletes the file
  - `--no-cache` skips both paths (this is at the pipeline-orchestrator level; here we just test the API)
  - 100 MB size cap evicts oldest-first
  - cache-key fast-check: same triple → same key; different triple → different key. All `@no-llm`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: README "Caching" section: 24 h TTL, location, how to clear (`rm -rf ~/.cache/yantra/ask/`), `--no-cache` flag.
- **Verify**: Tests pass; manually creating an entry with `created_at` 25 h ago and calling `get` returns `null` and the file is gone.

### TASK-011: `AskPipeline.run(query, opts)` orchestrator

- [ ] **Implementation**: `ask-pipeline.ts`. Class `AskPipeline` with constructor `{ searchProvider, fetcher, extractor, ruleBasedSummarizer, llmSummarizer (null | LlmSummarizer), cache, ethicsGate, events: EventEmitter, logger, clock }`. `run(query: AskQuery) → Promise<AskCard[]>`:
  1. `events.emit('task_started', { task_id, type: 'ask', query: query.raw, at: clock.now() })`.
  2. Compute `cacheKey`; if `!query.noCache`, try `cache.get(key)` — on hit, emit `task_completed` with `from_cache: true` and return immediately. **Warm path target: ≤ 1.5 s.**
  3. `events.emit('step_started', { step: 'search' })`. Call `searchProvider.search(query.normalized, { limit: query.limit + 2, signal })`. Top `query.limit` rows survive (the +2 is buffer for ethics refusals).
  4. For each `SearchResult` in parallel (with `Promise.allSettled`), bounded by `query.budgetCalls ?? query.limit`:
     a. `ethicsGate.checkUrl(url)` — on refusal, push a card with `notice: "this source was skipped: <reason>"`.
     b. `fetcher.fetch(url, { timeoutMs: query.perFetchTimeoutMs, signal })` — on timeout, push card with `notice: "fetch timed out"`.
     c. `extractor.extract(doc)` — on `null`, push card with `notice: "could not extract a readable article"`.
     d. Pick summarizer: `llmSummarizer ?? ruleBasedSummarizer`. Run summarize.
     e. Build `quotedSnippet` (first ≤ 280 chars of `contentText`, sentence-boundary-respecting).
     f. Build `AskCard`.
  5. Sort cards by `(success first, original rank ascending)` and slice to `query.limit`.
  6. `cache.put(key, cards)` (unless `noCache`).
  7. Write `outputs.json`, `cards/<i>.json`, `report.md` to the run dir.
  8. `events.emit('task_completed', ...)`. Return cards.

  Top-level `AbortController` with `query.pipelineBudgetMs` timeout aborts everything in flight; any in-flight results that haven't produced a card yet get a `notice: "pipeline budget exceeded"`.

- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `ask-pipeline.spec.ts` with full fake collaborators (no network, no browser). Scenarios:
  - happy path: 3 cards, sorted by rank, all summaries `rule-based`
  - cache hit: returns immediately, no search/fetch invoked
  - cache disabled by `--no-cache`: search/fetch still run
  - 1 ethics refusal + 2 ok: 3-card deck with 1 notice
  - 1 fetch timeout: timeout card + 2 ok
  - pipeline budget exceeded mid-fetch: partial deck with notice on missing rows
  - LLM summarizer present + `noLlm: true` query: rule-based wins (proves the seam respects the flag)
    All `@no-llm`.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: README adds a sequence diagram (ASCII) of the pipeline stages.
- **Verify**: All 7 scenarios pass; `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- ask-pipeline` clean.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

### Authentication & Secrets

- **No user authentication for the `ask` pipeline itself** — `ask` does not require login.
- **Search-API keys** (`tavily.api_key`, `brave.api_key`) live in the **OS keychain only** (memory §Security; plan §6). Never in `config.yaml`, never on disk in logs, never echoed in events. The keychain abstraction (FEAT-006) is the single read point.
- Every keychain read emits one line to `secrets.jsonl`: `{ key: "tavily.api_key", step_id: "search", ts }` — **value never recorded**.
- `yantra doctor` reports presence/absence of each key (not the value) so users can debug "why am I falling back to browser?"

### Error Handling

**Per-source failures appear as cards, not as task failures.** This is the headline design choice. A pipeline that fetches 3 sources where 1 fetch times out, 1 hits a robots refusal, and 1 succeeds returns a 3-card deck (1 success + 2 notice cards). The user sees the partial result and the reasons.

The only conditions that fail the whole task (exit code 2 + `task_failed` event + `report.md`):

- Search provider error AND no fallback succeeds (`SearchProviderError` from all available providers).
- All N fetches fail (deck is 100% notice cards) AND the user has not passed `--allow-empty`.
- Pipeline budget exhausted before a single card was produced.
- Programmer error / unhandled exception (caught at the top of `run`, logged, re-emitted as `task_failed`).

Custom error classes (extend `Error`, per memory §Error Handling):

- `SearchProviderError` (and subclasses `TavilyAuthError`, `RateLimitError`, `BrowserSearchError`) — carry `{ provider, host, statusCode, retryAfter }` context.
- `FetchError` — `{ url, kind: "timeout" | "http-status" | "network" | "too-large", statusCode? }`.
- `ExtractionError` — only used for truly broken HTML; normally `extract` returns `null`.
- `AskPipelineError` — the catch-all wrapper; always paired with a `task_failed` event.

### Logging

- `pino` (memory §Logging) at levels:
  - `info` — one line per stage transition (search-started, search-completed with N results, fetch-started for URL X, fetch-completed in M ms, etc.).
  - `warn` — recoverable failures (one fetch timed out; falling back from Tavily to browser because key missing).
  - `error` — task-aborting failures, paired with `task_failed`.
  - `debug` — per-fetch headers, redirect chain, extractor's pre-clean DOM stats, summarizer scores per sentence.
- All log lines dual-write to the run-dir's `events.jsonl` (memory §Logging).
- `TaskEvent` stream is the source of truth; logs are commentary (memory §Logging). Tests inspect events, not log output.
- Secret-shape redactor on the pino instance is the safety net for the keychain reads (defense-in-depth).

### Security

- **No content from this pipeline reaches an LLM in MVP.** The rule-based path has no LLM call. The LLM-summarizer seam is stubbed to `null` — the only way it returns non-`null` is FEAT-011 lighting it up via the feature gate.
- **When FEAT-011 lights up the seam**, the `LlmSummarizer.summarize(article, query)` implementation **must** pass `article.contentText` (and any other LLM-bound bytes) through `sanitizer.sanitize(payload, "public")` before calling `LLMClient.send` — enforced by the CI static-analysis grep on every `LLMClient.send` (memory §Security; plan §6). The `public` sanitization profile is appropriate because `ask` operates over public web content; `read-only-data` and `authenticated` profiles are for workflow-driven scopes (FEAT-009/010), not for `ask`.
- **Search-provider snippets are also untrusted** (provider could be compromised; remote could inject content). Any LLM-bound snippet must transit the sanitizer too — covered by the same grep rule.
- **Ethics gate is non-bypassable** (memory §Security): every fetch URL, including the single DuckDuckGo URL used by `BrowserSearchProvider`, transits the gate. No `--ignore-robots` flag exists in MVP.
- **Ephemeral profiles only.** `BrowserSearchProvider` and `BrowserFallbackFetcher` use `BrowserProvider`'s ephemeral mode (FEAT-003) — fresh user-data-dir per invocation, removed on success or error. No cross-query cookie bleed.
- **No literal credentials echo anywhere.** The `agent.jsonl` log records prompt + response when the LLM seam is lit; in MVP it stays empty for `ask`.
- **Cache-dir permissions 0700** on POSIX (best-effort on Windows). `yantra doctor` warns if world-readable.

### Testing

- **Headline path**: `@no-llm` E2E (`e2e/ask-no-llm.spec.ts`) is mandatorily passing on all three OSes × `LLM_PROVIDER=none`. This is the spine test for the agent-optional invariant.
- **`@requires-llm` path** (LLM-enhanced summarizer): tagged but **all `it.skip`** in this feature. FEAT-011 promotes them to `it()` once the real impl lands.
- **Mock strategy** (memory §Testing — mock external deps only, never internal logic):
  - `undici.MockAgent` for all HTTP — Tavily, Brave, fetcher.
  - `FakeBrowserProvider` in `packages/core/src/extraction/__fakes__/` — implements the BrowserProvider interface and serves fixtures.
  - `FakeKeychain` — in-memory map.
  - Real `@mozilla/readability`, real `cheerio`, real `jsdom`, real `Intl.Segmenter` — these are deterministic + fast, no mocking needed.
- **Property-based tests** (memory §Testing — non-optional for protocol-adjacent code):
  - `cache-key.spec.ts` — purity of the hash function.
  - `summarizer.spec.ts` — determinism of rule-based summarizer.
- **Integration tests against fixture HTML** — five fixtures cover Readability's known failure modes; the pipeline test runs end-to-end against the BBC fixture + a local HTTP fixture server.
- **CI matrix from day one** (memory §Testing) — 3 OSes × `{anthropic, none}`. The `none` legs are the canonical proof of the invariant.
- **Dogfooding criterion** (plan §9): the planner-author manually runs `yantra ask "today's top news"` on a fresh install and confirms a useful card returns in under 30 s.
